items.q: Two stories about the exchange Mt. Gox in 2014. On 28 February it filed for bankruptcy after admitting that about 850,000 bitcoin were gone. Filing: an untested file is not an empty one. Old file: whoever holds the keys holds the coins.
Filing: the network let the exchange spend the same coins twice. Old file: miners held the coins back for a fee.
Filing: customers lost their own keys. Old file: backups expire, so an old file can be thrown away.

source.locator: slide 11 'Release tags sort by number, not by letters' (11 of 42)

items.q: A script drops the release candidates from a list of release tags and compares the final releases sorted as text with the same releases sorted by version number. It adds up how far each tag moves between the two orders. Tips: release tag: the name of one version of a program, such as v3.1; release candidate: a test version before the final one; its tag carries rc; sorted as text: letter by letter, so "v28.0" comes before "v3.1". What does it print?
items.code:
tags = ['v28.0', 'v3.1', 'v28.0rc1',
        'v4.0', 'v24.2', 'v9.1']
final = [t for t in tags if 'rc' not in t]
def key(t):
    return [int(p) for p in t[1:].split('.')]
a = sorted(final)
b = sorted(final, key=key)
move = 0
for t in final:
    move += abs(a.index(t) - b.index(t))
print(move)
tips: the name of one version of a program, such as v3.1
a test version before the final one; its tag carries rc
letter by letter, so "v28.0" comes before "v3.1"
items.understanding: reason: why version tags must be sorted by number, not by text

items.q: The program reads five sequence values (a 32-bit number in each input). A value signals opt-in replacement when it is below 0xfffffffe and carries a relative timelock when bit 31 is clear. It adds up the low 16 bits of the values that do both. Tips: opt-in replacement: the unconfirmed payment may be replaced by one with a higher fee; relative timelock: the spent output must first wait a set time; bit 31: the highest of the 32 bits; clear means 0; 0x: starts a hexadecimal number. What does it print?
items.code:
seqs = [0xffffffff, 0xfffffffd, 0x0000001e,
        0x80000010, 0x00400005]
total = 0
for s in seqs:
    replace = s < 0xfffffffe
    timed = (s >> 31) == 0
    if replace and timed:
        total += s & 0xffff
print(total)

the spent output must first wait a set time
the highest of the 32 bits; clear means 0
